Winsorized binning

Source: R/rbin-winsorize.R
rbin_winsorize.Rd

Bin continuous data using winsorized method.

Usage

rbin_winsorize(
  data = NULL,
  response = NULL,
  predictor = NULL,
  bins = 10,
  include_na = TRUE,
  winsor_rate = 0.05,
  min_val = NULL,
  max_val = NULL,
  type = 7,
  remove_na = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'rbin_winsorize'
plot(x, print_plot = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or tibble.

response

Bare column name, character name, or variable holding a character name in data. A binary variable coded as 0/1, a logical variable, or a two-level factor/character. For a two-level factor the first level is treated as 0 and the second as 1. A character response is sorted in byte (C-locale) order: uppercase before lowercase, ASCII before accented characters; use a factor to choose the event level. The second value is the event. Rows with a missing response are dropped with a warning.

predictor

Bare column name, character name, or variable holding a character name in data. A numeric predictor; non-missing values must be finite. The values used to compute the cut points (after winsorizing) must have absolute value up to 1e300.

bins

Number of bins.

include_na

logical; if TRUE, a separate bin is created for missing values.

winsor_rate

A value from 0.0 to 0.5.

min_val

the low border, all values being lower than this will be replaced by this value. The default is set to the 5 percent quantile of predictor.

max_val

the high border, all values being larger than this will be replaced by this value. The default is set to the 95 percent quantile of predictor.

type

an integer between 1 and 9 selecting one of the nine quantile algorithms detailed in quantile() to be used.

remove_na

logical; if TRUE, missing values are removed while calculating quantiles. If FALSE, retained predictor values must not be missing; use TRUE to retain a separate missing-value bin.

x

An object of class rbin_winsorize.

print_plot

logical; if TRUE, prints the plot else returns a plot object.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

Value

A list of class rbin_winsorize with the following elements: bins, a data.frame with one row per interval (including empty intervals) and a final row for missing values when present; method; vars; lower_cut; upper_cut; and clamp, the fitted minimum and maximum used when scoring new data (absent if all predictor values are missing).

Examples

bins <- rbin_winsorize(mbank, y, age, 10, winsor_rate = 0.05)
bins
